title: Clear photos, short case studies and a free site
course_title: Online Portfolio Building: Show Your Best Work and Win Clients

say: Clear photos, short case studies, and a free site.
This is the video for module two of Online Portfolio Building.
For physical work, the photo is the work, as far as an online viewer is concerned. A great outfit in a dark, blurry photo looks like an average outfit.
You do not need a professional camera. A smartphone, window daylight and a sheet of white paper are enough.

say: Light is the most important thing. Place the item close to a window, with light coming from the side. Side light shows stitching, beading and icing.
Hold a sheet of white paper or a white plate on the dark side to soften the shadows. Keep the background plain.

panel.heading: Light makes or breaks the photo

say: Avoid harsh midday sun, which makes hard shadows. Turn off yellow ceiling bulbs, because mixed light gives strange colours.
And do not use the flash. It flattens texture and makes shiny spots on soap, glass or satin.

panel.heading: Light makes or breaks the photo

say: Wipe the lens first, because finger grease makes photos hazy. Then take an overall shot of the whole item, filling most of the frame.

panel.heading: Four photos for every piece
items: Overall: the whole item, straight on
Detail: the part that shows your skill
Scale: a hand or object to show size
In use: worn, served or displayed

say: Next a detail shot, close up on a hem, beadwork or piping. Tap the screen on the item to focus, and move closer instead of zooming.

say: A photo shows what you made. A case study explains why, how, and what difference it made. About 150 to 300 words is enough for a main piece.
For example, Bisi, a baker in Lagos. Problem: a mother wanted a football cake for 40 children in 4 days, at an outdoor party where buttercream could melt.

cards.d: What the customer needed, and the challenge: budget, deadline, size or special request.
The steps you took and why. Explain one or two choices. Name your part in team work.
What you delivered and what happened next: feedback, repeat orders, a testimonial.

say: Process: Bisi suggested firmer fondant, made the toppers two days ahead to dry hard, and sent a sketch on WhatsApp for approval before baking.

say: Result: the cake stayed firm through the 3-hour party, and the mother has since ordered two more. A new customer learns all that in under a minute.

say: One warning. Some people offer a free website, then ask for your email password, your BVN, or a payment to activate it. That is a scam. The real tools are free to sign up for directly.

say: To remember. Use soft side daylight, no flash and a plain background. Take overall, detail, scale and in-use photos.
Write each case study as problem, process and result, with honest results only. Choose one free main home, check it is shared, and guard your passwords.
